note: Conformance rules, first form (2026-11-10; Gavriel Technologies; direction of Luis Jake Gabriel III: the work must not go in circles or revert to conventional architectures, and every step is judged by whether performance improved and whether the system moved closer to the specification). Each rule names the specification section it protects (docs/2026-11-10-neumor-guide-how-it-works.md), how it is detected from the repository itself (source text, design files, assemblies; never from prose claims), the detector that runs it (nmtool::conformance), and the known violations it tolerates today (stand_ins), each with a recorded reason and the plan step that removes it (docs/2026-11-10-neumor-plan-whole-architecture.md section 5). recorded_state is the state written when the rule was added; the runner prints the live state beside it. A rule with must_pass_now true fails the run when it finds a violation that no stand-in covers, so a recorded stand-in does not block and a new violation does. Run: nmtool::conformance::cli.

rules.protects: 1 (no conventional transformer block as a structural unit); 8.4 (no regression to conventional architectures)
rules.detect: Every string literal in the served path (crates/nmapi/src) that names an engine assembly under designs/assemblies is a bound assembly. Each is followed through its base chain; it is the released layer order when its note, or its base's note, carries a mark of the reference generator (run s6 assemblies). Each such binding is a violation unless a stand-in records why.

stand_ins.reason: 2026-11-10: still bound by the shared sensory path that encodes each chunk once for every tentacle (layers 0 to the deepest drone layer in the released order, kept by content key) and by the Core Brain's exact reading paths; each tentacle's drone reads run through its own generated assembly (tentacle-t<n>, nmapi::tentacle_body). Along any one path the released order is the only order that keeps the weights' meaning without training (tentacle core design 1.1); the encoder is a candidate to move into a shared sensory module next.

rules.protects: 2.1, 3 (tentacles never exchange directly; G1 is the sole path); law 2
rules.detect: (a) The existing gates are present in source: the Core Brain bypass relation, the window crossover gate, one window per chunk. (b) Every assembly edge under designs/assemblies is checked with the bypass relation (an end inside one tentacle and the other end in another tentacle, or outside the Core Brain). (c) Call-graph text search over the files that define or import the unit and window types, outside the coordinating level: a unit or window struct holding a field of a unit or window type, or a function taking two of them (self counts inside their impl).

rules.protects: law 14 and rules.md standalone rule (nothing points outside the Nano folder)
rules.detect: No absolute path (a drive letter followed by a slash or backslash, or a user home folder; comment lines and a section check's fixtures from its fn check line on are skipped) in the code and configuration the Nano runs (crates source and manifests, designs, bin, .mcp.json, .cargo/config.toml, Cargo.toml); every Cargo path dependency resolves inside the folder; no top-level or second-level link leads outside.
